subject: Exact node mapping / VPC topology evidence for EU-only processing request
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medsys.eu>
To: lukas.meyer@redwood.inference.com
Cc: privacy@medsys.eu
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 16:32:00 +0200
Subject: Request: exact processing node mapping for EU-only commitment

Hi Lukas,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As part of our legal review we need a detailed map that ties Redwood’s EU-only processing commitment to exact compute nodes and VPC segments. Specifically:

- A list of physical/virtual node names (or instance identifiers) that will process MediSys EU traffic.
- The VPC/subnet IDs and AZs those nodes sit in.
- Network egress controls, whether traffic leaves the AZ/region for any maintenance tasks, and any managed services that reach outside the region.

Can you provide a short evidence bundle we can attach to our DPA file? Preferably a CSV for the node inventory and a topology PDF.

Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Security & Privacy, MediSys AG

From: lukas.meyer@redwood.inference.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medsys.eu>, privacy@medsys.eu
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.inference.com
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 09:11:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Request: exact processing node mapping for EU-only commitment

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide an evidence bundle that maps customer routing policies to dedicated node identifiers and VPC/subnet ranges. Quick clarifications:

1) Do you need host-level identifiers (hypervisor/instance ids) or logical node names (redwood-node-001)? Legal sometimes prefers logical names to avoid exposing low-level infrastructure.
2) Are we also including scheduled maintenance windows that potentially move workloads for patching (these are within the same region but may touch a control plane outside the region)?

I'll pull naomi and Rafael in to assemble the CSV and topology. We can also include short notes on our routing policy and the proof-of-residency stamp (signed manifest). Expect a first draft by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Lukas Meyer
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.inference.com
To: lukas.meyer@redwood.inference.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 10:04:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Request: exact processing node mapping for EU-only commitment

Team —

Attached are the files I compiled for MediSys: eu_node_inventory.csv and vpc_topology_diagram.pdf (attachments). The CSV contains: node_name, logical_id, instance_id, region, az, vpc_id, subnet_id, purpose, last_patched. I scrubbed hypervisor hostnames and only left instance_ids and logical node names to balance evidence with operational confidentiality.

Notes:
- All nodes listed are in the eu-west-1 region and live in customer-dedicated subnets (private).
- Control plane calls (metric collection, autoscale triggers) go to our control plane endpoints in eu-west-1 unless capacity overflow occurs — in overflow we failover to a pre-authorized EU replica pool. We documented the failover policy in the checklist (scp-evidence-checklist.xlsx).

Elena / MediSys team: if you need full hypervisor-level identifiers for audit, let us know — we'll need an NDA amendment to share that level of detail.

-Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Platform Engineering, Redwood Inference

(Attachment placeholders: vpc_topology_diagram.pdf, eu_node_inventory.csv, scp-evidence-checklist.xlsx)

From: Kieran Black <kieran.black@riskassess.io>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medsys.eu>, lukas.meyer@redwood.inference.com
Cc: privacy@medsys.eu
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 09:47:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Request: exact processing node mapping for EU-only commitment

Hi all —

Quick note from the external assessor: the CSV looks good for mapping and the topology diagram is clear. A couple of minor asks for our SOC/SIG evidence pack:

- Add a column in the CSV for "data_partition_tag" showing which tenant routing policy applied (MediSys-prod, MediSys-staging).
- Clarify in the topology PDF whether any management agents (patching, monitoring) have outbound TLS connections to non-EU endpoints and, if so, which ports and destinations they use.

If Redwood can add those two items we can close the evidence checklist and move to sign-off.

Cheers,
Kieran Black
Senior Assessor, RiskAssess Ltd.

From: lukas.meyer@redwood.inference.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medsys.eu>, Kieran Black <kieran.black@riskassess.io>
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.inference.com, jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 22:08:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Request: exact processing node mapping for EU-only commitment

Elena / Kieran —

Thanks for the quick review and the asks. Rafael updated the CSV to include data_partition_tag; Naomi added a short appendix in the topology PDF that lists outbound management endpoints and ports (all TLS 443 to eu-managed endpoints; no outbound to non-EU destinations except a telemetry collector in eu-central-1 owned by our EU partner).

I've uploaded the final package to our secure share: https://drive.redwood.com/s/secure/MediSys-EU-topology (shared to elena.rossi@medsys.eu). Also recording the artifacts in HUBSPOT-112233 for audit.

If you confirm this closes your checklist we'll mark the evidence bundle as delivered and attach to the DPA.

Best,
Lukas
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

(Attachments: vpc_topology_diagram.pdf, eu_node_inventory.csv, scp-evidence-checklist.xlsx)
